headline: A 2019 law confirms that certain donations and payments made for the families of the Virginia Beach shooting victims get specific tax treatment.
what_it_does: The law says cash gifts made on or after May 31, 2019, for the families of people killed or wounded in the Virginia Beach mass shooting count as tax-deductible contributions. It also says that certain payments by tax-exempt organizations to the spouses or dependents of those victims, made from May 31, 2019 through June 1, 2021, count as related to the organization's tax-exempt purpose. This applies only if the payments were made in good faith, used a reasonable and objective formula, and were applied consistently to the victims.

who_it_affects.group: Families of people killed or wounded in the May 31, 2019 Virginia Beach mass shooting
who_it_affects.how: Their spouses and dependents may receive cash support from donors and tax-exempt organizations that the law treats as tax-favored.

who_it_affects.group: People who gave cash to help the families of the Virginia Beach shooting victims
who_it_affects.how: Cash gifts made on or after May 31, 2019, for those families are treated as tax-deductible contributions.

who_it_affects.group: Tax-exempt organizations that paid victims' spouses or dependents
who_it_affects.how: Qualifying payments made from May 31, 2019 through June 1, 2021, are treated as related to their tax-exempt purpose rather than as benefits to private individuals.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed into law December 20, 2019, with the tax treatment applying retroactively to gifts and payments made starting May 31, 2019; the organization payment rule covers payments made through June 1, 2021.
